text:
samantha: FYI escalation from ACME-prod. They're seeing sustained ~700-900ms p95 and a billing spike. They claim traffic is pinned to us-west in their app but responses are coming from apac1. example request-id: req_20260304-abc123. Can someone take a look? :eyes:
akshay: On it. Can you paste the route/failover policy for that API key and a sample response header from a live request? Need X-Redwood-Region, X-Request-Id, any cookie values.
samantha: Pasting partial response headers from a live hit: ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-Id: req_20260304-abc123
X-Redwood-Region: apac1
Set-Cookie: rw_affinity=apac|v1; Domain=.acme.com; Path=/; Max-Age=86400``` Also exporting the policy from the console (sanitized): ```{
  "route": "acme-main",
  "sticky": "cookie",
  "priority": ["apac","us-west"],
  "weights": {"apac": "90", "us-west": "10"},
  "ttl": 86400
}``` This is odd because the UI previously showed us-west as primary.
akshay: Two red flags: weights are strings and priority array lists apac first. Runtime should respect explicit priority order unless weights are present and non-zero. Did a migration run recently?
emily: I pulled the audit log — there was a bulk migration last week that normalized weights from numbers to strings to preserve formatting, and a CSV import accidentally introduced a few non-breaking spaces into some weight values (e.g. "90\u00A0"). That can break numeric parsing. Our selection logic does: parseFloat(weight) and if parse fails we fallback to sort by weight descending but NaN handling is buggy.
samantha: Repro steps I ran locally to demonstrate: ```# force a request with us-west hint
curl -I -H "X-Region-Hint: us-west" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate``` response header still shows X-Redwood-Region: apac1.
akshay: Ok that matches. For mitigation, we can either strip weights (so runtime uses explicit priority order) or update weights to numeric values. Quick patch I can push: coerce weight strings with unicode trim before parseFloat and treat NaN as 0 instead of sending to top.
emily: I drafted a hotfix PR that normalizes weight tokens and rejects weird whitespace on policy writes. Also adding a policy validation rule in the console to prevent string-typed weights.
ops-bot: deploy:hotfix/weight-parse -> production queued (PR #4921). Rolling deploy in 3m.
akshay: Temp workaround for the customer: edit their route and remove the weights object (console -> routes -> acme-main -> advanced -> remove weights). That will force the runtime to use explicit priority order. Samantha, can you apply and test?
samantha: Removing weights now... applied. Re-running curl: ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-Id: req_20260304-abc129
X-Redwood-Region: us-west
Set-Cookie: rw_affinity=us-west|v1; Domain=.acme.com; Path=/; Max-Age=86400``` Looks good, latency back down to ~80ms for that request. Sending update to ACME support.
emily: Hotfix merged and deployed. Also creating INF-789: audit migration script and add assert that weights are numeric.
samantha: ACME confirmed reduced latency and billing spike stopped. They said their dashboards show normal region distribution now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
akshay: I'll follow up with a postmortem and add a console warning for mixed-type weights.
emily: Adding unit tests for the parse path and a small data-migration to backfill numeric weights.
ops-bot: ticket INF-789 created and assigned to @emily.
samantha: closing the escalation on our side; leaving INF-789 for follow-up. Thanks team.
